text:
Liz H.: heads up — ran into a Cloudflare Workers issue while onboarding the new js SDK sample app. auth/retry logic blows up at runtime: `ReferenceError: Buffer is not defined` and streaming fails with `TypeError: request body stream closed`.
Miguel: hmm, sounds like classic Node API bleed into an edge worker. Is the sample running unbundled or via esbuild/rollup?
Liz H.: unbundled repro in `samples/cf-worker` so easier to see errors. esbuild target was default (esnext).
Samir: CF Workers have no Buffer, no node:crypto, and slightly different streams. You need to build for webworker and replace node libs.
Liz H.: any minimal shim suggestions? I tried `import { Buffer } from 'buffer'` but the auth module still pulls `node:crypto` via a transitive package.
Miguel: two options: 1) use a tiny adapter that swaps the SDK's low-level crypto calls to globalThis.crypto.subtle for signing; 2) shim imports at bundle time with `--inject:buffer-shim.js` or alias `node:buffer` to `buffer` in bundler config.
Nina: for esbuild we put this in CI sample build: `esbuild src/index.ts --bundle --format=esm --platform=neutral --target=es2020 --outfile=dist/worker.js --inject=./shims/buffer.js` where `shims/buffer.js` exports Buffer from 'buffer'.
ops-bot: deploy-preview created for liz/sample-cf-fix #142 — running smoke tests. :rocket:
Samir: also watch out for AbortController differences. Cloudflare's AbortController works but some fetch polyfills expect `signal.throwIfAborted()` — avoid relying on Node-only helpers.
Liz H.: found another quirk: our retry backoff uses `setImmediate` in the SDK core; CF doesn't have that. I swapped to `queueMicrotask` fallback. Code: `const setImmediate = globalThis.setImmediate ?? (fn => queueMicrotask(fn));`
Miguel: good catch. For streaming: CF only exposes ReadableStream/TransformStream. If SDK uses Node stream.Transform it won't work. We added a tiny wrapper `node-stream-to-web` in the sample to convert.
Nina: typing note — consumers using `types: "module"` in package.json saw `Cannot use import statement outside a module` when Wrangler served the file. Our sample's workaround: ensure `wrangler.toml` has `type = "esm"` and the built artifact is ESM. Add a short note in the sample README.
Liz H.: I've pushed a branch with three things: esbuild config, buffer shim, and AbortController fallback. ops-bot shows preview passed smoke tests, but streaming still flaky in a few edge cases.
Samir: leave a failing test for streaming; that'll guide the runtime-specific fix. Also add a comment linking to the runtime compatibility matrix in docs.
Miguel: I can open an SDK PR to accept an optional `runtimes: ["node", "webworker"]` hint so the core can avoid Node-only APIs when building for webworker. That will keep code paths explicit.
Nina: I'll update the sample README with step-by-step wrangler/esbuild notes and a checklist: set `type = "esm"`, use `--inject` buffer shim, target `es2020`, and include AbortController fallback.
Liz H.: thanks y'all. Plan: Miguel PR for runtime flag, Nina docs, Samir adds failing streaming test, I'll tidy the sample and keep the preview until streaming green. :thumbsup:
Miguel: sounds good. tagging @eng-runtime for visibility.
ops-bot: CI for branch liz/sample-cf-fix completed: 12/13 checks passing (streaming-smoke failing).
Liz H.: logging the remaining streaming stack from preview: `TypeError: TransformStream is not constructible` — possibly because the worker environment injected a polyfill that isn't spec-compliant.
Samir: ok let's file an issue with the exact worker preview ID and the failing stack. I'll triage tomorrow morning.
Liz H.: created issue #987 with logs + preview link. Thanks everyone — will follow up in PR comments. :heart:
